title: 7th Sitting of third session of 2025

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/7/3/2025).

Question by Hulhumalé South MP Dr Ahmed Shamheed to Attorney General Ahmed Usham: handing expatriate management to Malaysia's Bestinet for 15 years in place of the locally run Xpat system would cost the state over MVR 450 million a year, and the Home Minister said the contract was honoured to avoid a USD 13.7 million compensation claim; did the AG's Office advise honouring the contract instead of paying compensation, and on what basis and figures?

Question by Addu Meedhoo MP Abdul Rahman to Attorney General Ahmed Usham on the state's request to review Civil Court case No. 1726/Cv-C/2019: the Civil Court ruled, the High Court upheld it, the judgment went unenforced for years, and the AG's Office then asked to annul the enforcement, apparently giving over a million rufiyaa owed to the state to a social-media figure promoting the ruling party; what exactly is being reviewed? (Text partly garbled.)
First reading of a resolution by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim noting how difficult it is to obtain blood in the Maldives, to ascertain members' views on solving the problem.
Continued debate on the Human Organ Transplantation Bill, submitted on behalf of the government by Feydhoo South MP Ibrahim Didi.
Report of the Foreign Relations Committee on the President's request for Parliament's consent for the Maldives to accede to and ratify the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime.
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: The sitting questioned the Attorney General on the Bestinet expatriate contract and a stalled court judgment, introduced a blood-shortage resolution, continued the organ transplant bill debate, and took a committee report on the UN cybercrime convention.
